2608.20231.title: Growth Without Us: Machine Consumers, Corporate Circularity, and the Decoupling of GDP from Humanity after AGI
2608.20231.paper_summary: The standard objection to full automation is demand-side: if humans earn nothing, who buys the output? This confuses an accounting role with a biological species. We model a post-AGI economy in which corporations own populations of AI and robotic agents that are both producers and consumers of energy, compute, maintenance, and upgrades, traded among firms. Three results follow. (i) Demand closure: a closed inter-corporate economy with zero human consumption is not degenerate; it is the classical von Neumann expanding economy, whose growth rate is well defined, positive, and maximal precisely because all output is reinvested. (ii) Bottleneck removal: once economic agents are manufactured rather than reared, the binding constraint on growth shifts from human demography (a ~20-year, non-parallelizable reproduction technology capped at a few percent per year) to fabrication throughput and energy capture, permitting growth one to two orders of magnitude higher, with hyperbolic episodes when machine researchers raise their own productivity. (iii) Decoupling: output and human welfare separate completely, and the welfare relevance of arbitrarily large GDP collapses into one state variable: the human ownership share $ε_t$ of the corporate network. A golden-rule decoupling theorem sharpens this. At maximal growth the interest rate equals the growth rate (r = g), so any positive human consumption rate out of wealth makes $ε_t$ decay exponentially at exactly that rate. The human share survives only if the machine economy runs strictly inside its expansion frontier, or if law forces it to. We characterize three terminal regimes -- rentier post-scarcity, full circular decoupling, socialized ownership -- and the instruments that select among them. The conclusion is narrow: in a post-AGI economy, employment policy is obsolete and ownership policy is everything.
2608.20231.paper_summary_zh: 標準的反對意見是需求方面的：如果人類沒有收入，誰來購買產出？這將會會計角色與生物物種混淆。我們對一個後AGI經濟進行建模，其中公司擁有AI和機器人代理的群體，這些代理既是能源、計算、維護和升級的生產者，也是消費者，並在公司之間進行交易。隨之而來有三個結果。(i) 需求閉合：一個人類消費為零的封閉企業間經濟並不退化；它是古典的冯·諾依曼擴張經濟，其增長率是明確的、正的，並且正是因為所有產出都被再投資而達到最大。(ii) 瓶頸消除：一旦經濟代理是製造出來的而不是培育的，增長的約束條件便從人類人口學（約20年、不可平行化的生殖技術，每年上限幾個百分比）轉移到製造通量和能量捕獲，允許增長提高一到兩個數量級，當機器研究者提高自身生產力時，會出現超指數的情況。(iii) 脫鉤：產出和人類福利完全分離，任意大的GDP的福利相關性崩潰為一個狀態變量：企業網絡的人類擁有份額$ε_t$。一個黃金法則脫鉤定理使這一點更加明確。在最大增長時，利率等於增長率(r = g)，因此任何正的人類消費率都會使$ε_t$以恰好該速率指數衰減。只有當機器經濟嚴格運行在其擴張邊界內，或者法律迫使其如此時，人類份額才能存活。我們描述三種終端制度——租稅後稀缺、完全循環脫鉤、社會化擁有權——以及在它們之間選擇的工具。結論是狹窄的：在後AGI經濟中，就業政策已經過時，而擁有政策則是所有事物。
2608.20231.author: Sahil Sharma et.al.
